name: lives
title: Lives
description: How many attempts a player has left, drawn as a pill of dots beside the number. A thin wrapper over stat and, since the presentation prop, an genuinely thin one: the number, the label, the change beside it, the announcement and the dots themselves are all stat's, and lives adds the kind, the component name and the silhouette. `value` is lives remaining and `max` the total, so zero is a real state and reads as "lives, 0 of 3" with three dashed dots still drawn, because a player should be able to see what they had. A life just lost is `delta={-1}`, not a state of its own. A held life is a solid dot and a spent one is the same circle left empty and dashed, so fill, stroke style and weight all differ and the loss survives colour blindness, a muted tab and reduced motion. Performs nothing: it does not take a life or decide when one left is critical.
docs: Pass `value` as lives remaining and `max` as the total; the dots are drawn from those two numbers and nothing else carries them, so there is one source of truth for one count. Pass `delta={-1}` on the render after a life goes, and stat renders the change beside the number. Pass `critical` when the host decides the player is down to the last of them; stat turns its own number and glyph and the dots follow, with no second attribute. The dots are `aria-hidden`, because stat already announces "lives, 1 of 3" and announcing them again would read the number twice. There is no stylesheet of its own: `presentation="dots"` is drawn by `@gamestage/stat`, which lives already depends on. Pass `presentation` to draw the number some other way; `dots` is the default because it is what the design draws.
